description.narrative: IFC anticipates that the Project will improve the quality and availability of financing for small and mid-market enterprises in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting their growth and expansion. Through longer-tenor and flexible private credit solutions, the Fund is expected to address a structural financing gap not adequately served by traditional bank lending. Beyond project-level outcomes, IFC expects the Project to contribute to greater market competitiveness by supporting the development of private credit as an alternative financing channel and mobilizing institutional capital into underserved segments. This is expected to enhance the resilience and diversification of capital markets in the region.

The proposed project consists of an IFC investment of up to EUR 20 million in ACP Credit II SCA SICAV-RAIF (ACP II or the Fund), a closed-end private credit fund targeting investments in Poland, Romania, and other countries in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE). The Fund will be domiciled in Luxembourg with a target size of EUR 250 million. The Fund will target established SMEs and mid-market corporates, providing financing for growth capex, acquisitions, buy-outs, and working capital needs.
